features.feature_value: Supports keeping speech in general but allows removal for hate speech or threats of violence.
features.evidence_span: "I believe in free speech, unless it is very hateful hate speech or threats of violence."
features.rationale: The participant states a conditional free-speech rule tied to hate/violence threats.

features.feature_value: Inclined to keep both unless content explicitly incites violence or is very profane; convictions about allowing speech with clear exceptions.
features.evidence_span: "allowing speech unless it explicitly incites violence or is very profane."
features.rationale: They describe specific disqualifying thresholds (incitement/very profane).

features.feature_value: Removed when it referenced “killing” or used excessive cursing that sounded like a call to violence.
features.evidence_span: "reference \"killing\"... or used excessive cursing that sounded like call to vilolience"
features.rationale: They explicitly link certain words/styles to violence intent cues for removal.

features.feature_value: If claims weren’t true or weren’t backed by facts, they removed both; misinformation drives removal.
features.evidence_span: "If anything was not true or actually backed up factually, I removed them both."
features.rationale: Their criterion is factual verification; false/unsupported claims lead to removal.

features.feature_value: Influence came from noticing extreme tradeoffs (one extreme + one normal) and that misinformation existed, making the moderation approach seem wrong.
features.evidence_span: "blatent misinformation"..."I either have to ok two possibly extreme views, or... ok 1 extreme view and one view that's relatively normal."
features.rationale: They criticize the decision process/approach while mentioning misinformation and extreme framing.

features.feature_value: Would allow posting if phrased respectfully; remove if it was just insulting someone with no reason.
features.evidence_span: "If put in a respectful way if would let them post it. If it was just insulting a person for no reason"
features.rationale: They give a stylistic/normative distinction (respect vs pointless insults) tied to posting decisions.

features.feature_value: Kept when mostly civil; removed when it seemed like complete rumors.
features.evidence_span: "If posts seemed mostly civil... If they seemed like complete rumors, they needed to go."
features.rationale: They describe two observable cues (civility and rumor-ness) guiding keep/remove.

features.feature_value: Says the construction/validity of arguments mattered; poorly voiced opinions on either side weren’t worth debating.
features.evidence_span: "The construction and validity of each argument. Poorly voiced opinions on either side do not seem worthwhile debating"
features.rationale: Their reflection emphasizes evaluating argument validity/quality rather than only content cues.
